checks.source_locations: Publisher PDF25/printed57, Theorem4.1; Section10 formulas; Blomer-Khan arXiv1804.01602v1 p1 and Wu arXiv v5 pp2-3.
checks.reason: Theorem4.1 quantifies over every cubic number field, but the directly inspected Blomer-Khan Theorem1 assumes prime level and primitive central character. T^3-5T+1 has no rational root, discriminant473=11*43, nonsquare positive discriminant, and squarefree polynomial discriminant; its field therefore has that composite discriminant and Artin conductor473. Its mod2 inert and mod3 mixed types also meet an S3 local restriction. This disproves the applicability of the cited prime-level theorem to the asserted generality, not the L-value bound itself. The cyclic case is handled separately in the source.
checks.counterevidence_and_repair: Wu v5 Corollary1.5 has saving (C(pi)/C(omega))^(-(1-2theta)/56) C(omega)^(-1/224). With theta=7/64, 25/1792>1/224, and C(omega) bounded by C(pi), this supplies the weaker saving1/224 with appropriate conductor/time dependence. The Section10 formulas then give112/167 and169/224, conditional on repairing the other inputs. The full cited journal Blomer-Khan version was not obtained; its equivalence to v1 is not asserted. This is an essential uniform-input justification gap affecting the advertised numerical improvements, not an absence theorem for all possible subconvexity results.

checks.source_locations: Publisher PDF34-35/printed66-67, equation(35), Table1 and Proposition5.2; PDF48/printed80, Lemma6.9; Taniguchi-Thorne publisher PDF52, Corollary8.15.
checks.reason: For n=p^2 and the indicator of the zero class modulo p^2, the printed functional is p^-8 c_p(0)=p^(-22/3). Scaling f=p^2 g is a bijection on the relevant GL2(Z) orbits, preserves stabilizers, and multiplies discriminants by p^8. Thus the true Shintani series is p^(-8s) times the original and the nonzero residue at5/6 scales by p^(-20/3), contradicting Proposition5.2. The witness can use p=5 with fixed inert7/mixed11 support, so irreducibility/S3 restrictions do not remove it.
checks.counterevidence_and_repair: The independently checked switching identity for the nonmaximal mass gives p^(-5/3)+p^-2-p^(-11/3), in agreement with the directly viewed external Corollary8.15. The printed mod-p pullback instead gives p^-2+p^(-7/3)-p^(-13/3); with t=p^(-1/3) their difference is t^5(1-t^2)(1-t^6)>0. True maximal secondary mass is (1-p^-2)(1-p^(-5/3)), not the printed (1-p^-2)(1-p^(-7/3)). The prime-level table is not thereby refuted. The higher-modulus extension and the secondary sieve constants require correction; a fixed nonzero X^(5/6) discrepancy is not absorbed by the smaller fixed-modulus error. Local corrections alone do not certify the complete uniform argument.

checks.source_locations: Publisher PDF46/printed78, definition of chi_Sigma on all p-adic cubic orders and claimed factorization through r_Sigma.
checks.reason: Take Sigma_infinity complex, Sigma_7 unramified inert and Sigma_11 unramified mixed. The irreducible forms g=x^3-2y^3 and h=x^3-15y^3 have negative nonsquare discriminants. Their mod7 cubic root counts are0 and3, while each has exactly one mod11 root and no repeated root. Hence chi_Sigma(g)=1 and chi_Sigma(h)=0. For every positive integer M the twisted GL2(Q_p) action of M I sends f to Mf, leaving its generic Q_p-algebra unchanged, but Mg and Mh are both zero modulo M. Therefore this generic-algebra indicator on all orders cannot factor through any fixed modulus.
checks.counterevidence_and_repair: Finite congruence conditions can describe suitable restrictions on maximal orders; that is a narrower domain than the one used in the switching/sieve argument. An extension from maximal orders changes the weights on nonmaximal orders and needs new switching and residue justification. The example remains irreducible and nonsingular and is not repaired by excluding the zero-discriminant locus. The Major rating concerns the essential passage to congruence functions, not falsity of the final field-count statements.

checks.source_locations: Publisher PDF68-70/printed100-102, Proposition9.11; equation(62), Lemmas9.8-9.10; BTT author-hosted33-page PDF pp2-3, Theorem1.3 and Table1.
checks.reason: The proof applies the first-prime cancellation of Lemma5.9 to lambda_(ell_1) with ell=rad(ell_1), although lambda_(p^2) has positive mean of order one. The root independently checked the retained-range witness: 0<kappa<1/100, a=kappa/10, epsilon=kappa/100; prime Q, X=Q^8, p of size X^a, q=q1=Q, m=m1=1, k=Q^2, n=ell1=p^2, n1=1. All stated coprimality, powerful/cubefree and border-range conditions hold, and n is below the later truncation X^(1/2+epsilon)/k.
checks.decisive_lower_bound: Equation(62) gives e_(Q,2)=1-1/Q or1 for every index-Q order. At p the order is maximal and the five splitting types give lambda_(p^2)=3,1,0,1,0. The kernel argument is O(X^(2a-1/4)) tending to zero, so Re V>=1/2 uniformly on the fixed nonnegative smoothing support. BTT's independently inspected local-condition theorem gives c_(Q,p)Y+O(Y^(5/6)+(Qp)^(2/3)Y^(2/3+tau)), Y=X^(3/4), for fields totally split at Q,p and in the fixed real S3 family (inert7,mixed11), with c_(Q,p) bounded below. The three index-Q suborders are distinct because an S3 cubic field has trivial automorphism group. Their contribution is at least(9/2)(1-1/Q) times that count, hence Re LHS is bounded below by a positive multiple of X^(3/4); all remaining contributions have nonnegative real part.
checks.contradiction_and_repair: The printed upper bound has exponents3/4-a+epsilon,5/8+kappa/3-a/3+epsilon,1/4+a+9kappa+epsilon,3/4-kappa+epsilon, each strictly below3/4. Exact rational coefficient checks were run independently. This is an asymptotic contradiction inside the intended application, not a numerical extrapolation. It enters(64), Propositions9.13-9.14, Theorem9.15, Corollary9.16 and the comparison used for Theorem9.1/Section10. As counterevidence to an asserted false main theorem, writing ell1=A B with A first-power primes and B powerful gives corrected residue savings A^-1,A^(-1/3) and Fourier weight W=A rad(B)^2<=ell1. The displayed sums have bounds L^epsilon,L^(1/6),L^(3/2). These preserve some aggregate exponents but do not repair local overlaps, fixed specifications or the other residue/congruence problems. BTT's full proof is an external input, not independently reproved.

checks.source_locations: Publisher PDF48/printed80, A^max definition; PDF58-59/printed90-91, equations(54)-(55) and Proposition8.4.
checks.reason: The additive Haar integral defining t_Sigma has t_Sigma(1)=D_Sigma, the positive product of local allowed maximal masses, rather than1. If a_p(j) is the raw local moment and m_p=a_p(0), then t(n)=D_Sigma product_(p^j||n) a_p(j)/m_p and T(s)=D_Sigma product_p F_p(s) with F_p(s)=sum_j(a_p(j)/m_p)p^(-js). The printed ordinary Euler factor uses global t(p^j) repeatedly and is not this Dirichlet series.
checks.counterevidence_and_repair: At unspecified primes m_p=(1-p^-2)(1-p^-3), the normalized first and second coefficients are p/(p^2+p+1) and p(p+1)/(p^2+p+1). Since the remaining coefficients have size at most j+1, (1-p^-2s)F_p(s)=1+O(p^(-1-sigma)+p^(-2-2sigma)+p^(-3sigma)), normally and absolutely for sigma>1/3. The local Artin factors are positive at p^-1/2, giving positive residue D_Sigma/2 times product_p(1-p^-1)F_p(1/2). Thus the corrected normalization proves the claimed analytic continuation and positive pole for the originally defined T. The implicit constants C_Sigma=alpha Res(T) and the derivative expression use that same series and remain valid. This verified scope, rather than repairability alone, supports Minor.

checks.source_locations: Publisher PDF41/printed73 Proposition6.1 and PDF43 Theorem6.5, before the later S3 support restriction.
checks.reason: For q=2 choose a smooth test supported sufficiently near discriminant4 with value1 there. The unweighted left side has one isomorphism class: the three index2 subrings of Z^3 are conjugate under S3, represented by xy(x-2y), discriminant4. There is no alternative maximal cubic algebra of discriminant1: the field case violates the degree3 Minkowski bound and the Q times quadratic case would need quadratic discriminant1. The right side has the discriminant1 split algebra, represented by xy(x-y), with three projective roots modulo2, so its value is3; all q^4-scaled terms vanish. A fresh finite calculation found exactly three unital dimension2 subalgebras of F2^3 and one S3 orbit.
checks.counterevidence_and_repair: Automorphism weights give1/2 on each side: the index2 order has automorphism group of size2 and Z^3 has size6. The later S3-supported applications have trivial stabilizers and avoid this particular obstruction. The scope-limited counting identity is false as printed, but this example does not invalidate the actual S3 application or repair P02/P03. The Minor rating is retained on that explicit dependency boundary.

checks.source_locations: Publisher PDF45-46/printed77-78, Theorem6.6 and its switching proof.
checks.reason: The theorem allows complex tensor invariant S3-functions, simple at d=(q,n), with phi_p(0)=0, without a norm bound. Its proof extracts phi_d(1^2 1), but the displayed error contains only the Fourier norm of phi_(n/d). Set n=5*7*11, q=d=5; choose the type1^2 1 indicator at5, inert support at7, mixed support at11, and multiply only the5-factor by arbitrary M. The stated hypotheses are preserved and the printed error is independent of M. For the unscaled tensor and negative discriminant, a=alpha^- A_n^(q)>0 and c=-gamma^- C_n^(q)>0. Choose smooth nonnegative Psi supported in(b/2,b), where 0<b<min(1,(c/(2a))^6), and X=1. The counting side is0, but the printed main expression M[a int Psi-c int x^(-1/6)Psi] is nonzero with size proportional to M, a contradiction to the claimed uniform error.
checks.counterevidence_and_repair: This tests the theorem's own printed coefficient, independently of P02's corrected secondary functional. Multiplying the error by |phi_d(1^2 1)| or imposing a suitable unit norm fixes this amplitude omission. In the later ordinary lambda_(p^j) application the value at type1^2 1 is1, so this extra factor does not enlarge that particular error. The report correctly retains this as Minor and does not present it as a new counterexample to the principal result.
